{"id":14344,"tenderTitle":"ARGONAUT LDE – Quick passivation system design","tenderNumber":"25.THIT.017","tenderDescription":"Argonaut LDE (previously named EL3, European Large Logistics Lander), is one of the keystones of the “Terrae Novae” exploration capabilities presented at Council Meeting 2022. Argonaut LDE aims at enabling a substantial and sustained European presence on the surface of the Moon ensuring Europe remains a key player in space exploration. Argonaut LDE aims at providing an autonomous European capability for regular large robotic surface missions for an extended duration. This provides the possibility to conduct independent missions if required as well as being a significant and visible contribution to the international sustainable exploration of the lunar surface.

The mission is designed to support both human and robotic exploration by providing a multipurpose lander known as the Lunar Descent Element (LDE):

•	Lunar Descent Element (LDE): 
o	A recurring lander, common to all ARGONAUT LDE missions. 
o	Designed to be compatible with different delivery missions without undergoing modifications; 
o	The LDE provides the functions of Payload transport to the Moon’s surface as well as the main mission functions common to all the different missions. 

The LDE is equipped to deliver various payloads through a mission-specific interface, typically referred to as the Cargo Platform Element (CPE). For the purpose of clarity the CPE and the related Payload are subject to a separate procurement under ESA’s responsibility. 
Thales Alenia Space Italy, have been Contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the Argonaut Lunar Descent Element (LDE) which will be used for the first mission in 2031. 
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the Argonaut LDE Quick passivation system design.

For safety reasons, the LDE shall provide quick passivation function of propellant tanks to avoid hypergolic explosion in case of accidental events. 
The passivation system shall work in all the mission phases, starting from launch through the spacecraft mission (once separated from the LV), until Lunar orbit insertion.

The main critical aspect is related to the timeframe and the reaction time needed, which is in the order of ms for the first mission phases, and seconds during third stage LV phase and space mission. 
The Contractor main tasks are :
• Perform trade-offs and analysis to evaluate and recommend the design solutions/architecture to ensure timely passivation of the Tanks.
• Highlight any aspect related to operational safety constraints.
• Prepare the documentation necessary to justify the test conditions, if any, established for development/qualification tests on Earth and correlation of the results with the corresponding environmental conditions seen by LDE in the realistic worst-case scenario.

The procurement of the Primary and Secondary Structures will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).

Procedure title: Quality Assessment and Red Parcel management in the GSA and AMS for 2024-2027
Description: The Netherlands Enterprise Agency (NEA) serves as an EU-delegated body responsible for the implementation of EU policies in the Netherlands. This mandates NEA to effectively and efficiently oversee compliance with EU regulations, particularly in relation to subsidies under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). Therefore, NEA is looking for a Contractor to facilitate the annual obligatory Quality Assessments (QAs). These QAs pertain to the Area Monitoring System (AMS) and the Geospatial Aid Application (GSA), including rigorous sample controls integral to the Programmatic Enforcement Cycle for interventions such as the BISS, the Eco scheme, the AECM, and various conditionalities, all integral parts of the CAP. Furthermore, the Contractor will be responsible for evaluating agricultural activities on parcels that yield results from the AMS, colloquially referred to as 'red parcels'. Both the QA and the processing of 'red parcels' involve a manual inspection relying on optical imagery. The Tendering Authority has estimated a total Contract value (including the optional extension years) exclusive of indexation of EUR 3,000,000 (exclusive of VAT). This estimated value should be understood as strictly an indication from which no rights can be derived. Because certain volumes are uncertain such as the number of red-parcels to be detected, or potential changes in EU legislation concerning the QAs. The estimated value is based on the costs of similar activities in the past years and the changed rules concerning the QA. This Tender Document was created using up-to-date knowledge and insights valid at the time of its formulation.
Lot description: In order to be able to execute the QA AMS, GSA and process the ‘Red Parcels’, the contractor will need to deliver the following products: 1)Transferring/handling of geospatial data such as Sentinel, Planet Fusion; 2)Make available a web-based viewer: the availability of a cloud in which all data can be accessed and production can run; 3)Computer Assisted Photo Interpretation (CAPI) environment; 4)Activities related to archiving of production data according to the conditions that are set by the European Commission. The scope of the Quality Assessment and the handling of 'red parcels' is to assess the quality of the information declared by the farmer as well as the quality of the automatic generated AMS-results. If a discrepancy is found between what the farmer declared or what the AMS yielded as a result and the information collected using remote sensing data, the application of the farmer will be modified accordingly and possible financial corrections can incur. All findings will be communicated to the scheme applicants. The communication will be facilitated through the RVO.nl platform hosted and provided by NEA. € 3,000,000,
